name: King's Indian Defense
description: A hypermodern course that teaches the default Nf6-g6-Bg7 setup first, then simple responses to White's common structures.

branches.title: Main Line: Fianchetto Setup
branches.description: Learn the default King's Indian starting structure.

moves.title: White starts d4
moves.explanation: White controls central squares. d4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The King Indian reaches a tense center: Black castles, then strikes with e5 or c5 after development.

moves.title: Watch the center
moves.explanation: Nf6 develops and pressures e4 without occupying the center yet. Nf6 develops a knight to f6. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.title: White expands
moves.explanation: White gains more space. c4 changes the central structure. Central pawn moves should either claim space, challenge an enemy pawn, or open a line for a piece. The King Indian reaches a tense center: Black castles, then strikes with e5 or c5 after development.

moves.title: Prepare bishop
moves.explanation: g6 prepares a bishop on g7 to pressure the long diagonal. g6 is a practical improving move for Black. In real games, keep asking: is my king safe, are my pieces active, and what central pawn break comes next?

moves.title: White supports center
moves.explanation: White reinforces central control. Nc3 develops a knight to c3. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.

moves.explanation: Bg7 activates the bishop. Next plans include castling and central breaks. Bg7 develops a bishop to g7. Developed pieces control central squares, help castling, and make future tactics possible without forcing anything too early.
